method_limits: Linux elapsed is high-resolution subprocess launch-to-completion time including I/O; CPU and RSS are native wait4 observations, with RSS KiB multiplied by1024.
Split-family observations sum elapsed/CPU across sequential family processes and use the maximum constituent RSS.

All25 cases retain six pairs and excluded warmups. No paired median elapsed or RSS increase exceeded5%, so no followup was selected. Individual above5% observations remain preserved and listed separately.
Small or noisy elapsed deltas are inconclusive; the sparse1,000,002-entry case is a synthetic stress control, not a traffic-model claim.

All24 tiny B/C pairs have equal peak RSS, across four rising levels(25,063,424 to25,456,640 bytes). This pattern is consistent with an inherited parent high-water floor in fork/exec wait4 measurement; it does not prove equal application-only memory. No new RSS control experiment was performed.
